meta.notes: 9-week nutrition plan bridging White River -> Vermont 50K. Arnon: 50M, 175 lb / 79 kg, 5'10. BASELINES ARE NOW RACE-PROVEN (per debrief section 6 + updated profile — the old 'gut untested beyond 3:20' premise is retired): ~210-230 cal/hr at 30-min GU Roctane cadence over 8 h with zero GI failure; SaltStick 1/45 min cool-weather, zero cramping; ~500 ml/hr fluid at 14-22 C (600-800 for heat); 3 caffeine gels from mile 18, clean. RACE TARGET for Vermont: step up to 240-260 cal/hr at 25-30 min cadence — tested on the 9/13 dress rehearsal; the proven floor is the fallback, never the ceiling abandoned. THEMES THIS BLOCK: (1) COLLAGEN PROTOCOL is the P1 nutritional lever — 15 g collagen + 250 mg vitamin C 30-60 min before every lower/tendon session, and daily with the foot-corrective block on other days (small daily doses beat one large dose; synthesis has a refractory window). (2) PROTEIN HIGH THROUGHOUT: 1.7-1.9 g/kg (~140-150 g) every day including rest days — tendon remodeling at 50 is protein-hungry. (3) NO NSAIDs around loading sessions (blunts collagen remodeling); fish oil is the sanctioned anti-inflammatory support. (4) Recovery weeks 1-2: calories modest, protein and collagen priority. (5) Real aid-station food remains UNTESTED — Vermont is raced self-supplied (gels + pretzels + SaltSticks carried), aid stations for water only. Day types match the new weekly skeleton (Sunday long runs, Tue hill+lower double, Thu easy+tendon double). date_overrides remain the source of truth for race week.
